items.title: Palworld is not Pokémon … and that’s the point
items.summary: While most people spent their summer break finding ways to escape the heat, I spent mine building bases, catching creatures and exploring a world that kept me coming back every single day and night. Over 200 hours later, Palworld has become my most played game in my Steam library. It may look like Pokémon at...
items.content:
While most people spent their summer break finding ways to escape the heat, I spent mine building bases, catching creatures and exploring a world that kept me coming back every single day and night.

Over 200 hours later, Palworld has become my most played game in my Steam library. It may look like Pokémon at first glance, but there is so much more to it beyond catching creatures.

The big selling point for both games is running around a world and capturing creatures of different species. Palworld even has its own ball throwing mechanic similar to Pokémon; but after investing an entire summer into the game, calling Palworld “Pokémon with guns” is nothing more than a weak analogy.

The biggest difference is how the aspect of creature collecting is used in the games.

In Pokémon, catching creatures is at the forefront of the game. One of the main goals is to capture every single Pokémon and complete the pokedex, hence the slogan “Gotta catch ‘em all,” whereas Palworld is a survival game first and a creature collecting game second.

In Palworld, catching a new creature, or Pal, as it’s called in the game, can mean so much more than just having a new fighter on your team.

Pals can be used to help you build up your base by collecting resources, planting crops, transporting materials and manufacturing items. Some Pals are great for fighting and exploring, while others are essential for upgrading your base and completing mundane tasks within the game.

Instead of just seeing which creatures are the strongest in the game, Palworld drives you to find which pals are best for your overall survival.

I wasn’t just collecting Pals for the sake of completing a collection; I was catching Pals that would benefit me best for specific needs. Chikipi was never going to be strong enough to take on a boss battle, but it was great for producing essential food items at the base so my character and Pals wouldn’t starve and I wouldn’t have to waste precious time looking for food.

This is what makes Palworld so different from Pokémon. The Pals are much more than just tools for combat, and make the game feel less like a turn-based fighting game and more like an open world survival.

Pokémon shows their creatures as friends and partners, while Palworld doesn’t share that sentiment. Pals can fight, work, hunt or even become resources for survival. The game doesn’t hold back in putting you in a world where survival takes priority over being nice.

It also gives you so much freedom. Pokémon has a streamlined path to it. Explore an area, catch Pokémon, battle trainers, get badges and move on to the next gym to eventually beat the elite four and become the new champion. Palworld gives you a world and lets you decide what you want to do with it.

With this freedom, you can come back to it and spend each session doing something different. I could log in one day and spend it working on my base, and the next day spend it exploring a new area or progressing in the story.

These aspects are what make the comparison of these games so misleading.

items.title: Pokemon-channeling Palworld courts fans through addictive play
items.summary: It would be fair to say that I’ve been out of the loop on AAA games the last few years. Big studios pushing wildly expensive product on a mostly cynical
items.content:
It would be fair to say that I’ve been out of the loop on AAA games the last few years. Big studios pushing wildly expensive product on a mostly cynical audience growing more cynical by the day did not exactly inspire confidence.

Especially when a single game costs somewhere in the ballpark of $70 (and developers think that’s too low — see speculation of GTA VI’s eventual price tag later this year). The last time I paid full price for a game was the Resident Evil 4 Remake, which took me back to pre-ordering the original for the Gamecube back in 2005.

Pokemon fans have long known that the price of a game does NOT go down over time. Nintendo fans in general accept this as something of an axiom. I played the original generation in 1998 quite a bit. Heck, I got an emulator, ROM and printed guide/walkthrough so that I could play and beat the second generation in Japanese before it came to North America.

Suffice it to say, I was a big Pokemon fan. I was out until, to quote Michael Corleone, they “pulled me back in” through a friend. That would’ve been the sixth generation around 2014 or so. I got a 3DS, Pokemon X and found myself reliving part of my childhood. I enjoyed the seventh generation, even if they occasionally seemed to run out of ideas, such as the introduction of a sandcastle Pokemon (they had earlier made an ice cream Pokemon, as well).

Then they moved from the 3DS to the Switch, which I don’t have. Pokemon had always been a handheld game, so the move seemed like an odd decision. That being said, The Pokemon Company empire knows what it is doing. Other AAA games take somewhere around $200 million or more to develop and can easily flop or merely break even. A Pokemon game costs around $10 to $20 million to develop and can generate around $1.5 billion in direct game sales.

It seemed they were indestructible, untouchable and what’s more is they knew it. Forget quality, just slap the name Pokemon on the product and it would sell like hotcakes. What could possibly go wrong?

Enter Palworld, “Pokemon with guns,” made by rival Japanese indie company Pocketpair as an open-world adventure game populated by “Pals,” which the player can battle or capture for combat, base building or traversal.

The early access version was released in January 2024 and reached a total number of players exceeding 25 million within one month. It peaked at more than 2 million concurrent players shortly after launch, something most AAA games never achieve.

Since the 1.0 full release July 10, it has roughly 400,000 concurrent players at any given moment on Steam. Critics (and Pokemon fans) point to the drop from the peak numbers, but those numbers for a game that released more than two years prior is nearly unheard of.

It’s also currently on Steam for $30, which for something of this magnitude and scope is quite the deal.

Jumping in, I initially had a feeling that Palworld’s core gameplay mechanics were similar to Minecraft, though I wouldn’t really know firsthand. You punch the tree to get wood, you punch the rock to get stone, then make a woodcutting axe and pickaxe with the materials you just gathered, improving your capabilities, build a home base and expand from there, rinse and repeat.

The slow grind and requirement that you (or your industrious Pals) craft everything yourself really gives weight to everything. You didn’t just find those cold-resistant clothes in a chest, you had to make them yourself. You can build a ranch, capture some of the sheep-like Pals and they will drop wool. Or you can go fight wild ones, who drop wool and lamb chops for cooking later.

I can’t be the only one who always thought about eating some of the cute little monsters in Pokemon. After all, who wouldn’t want to try some Magikarp sushi? In Palworld, your monster buddies need to eat, too. Morality aside, you can feed bacon to the pigs, if you get my drift.

To repeat myself, I do not own a Nintendo Switch or its aptly-named successor, The Switch 2, so I have not been able to play the newer Zelda games, but the climbing, hang gliding and stamina management seem copied directly, from what I know. You would think Nintendo would get litigious, which brings me to the next point.

I'm practically a Palpagos real estate agent now, and like any good agent, I've prepared a few listings for your own base tours—though my editor says I'm not allowed to charge the typical fees associated with such a service. Recent updates August 14, 2026: I've added a new base location for farming ore and coal in the early game. It's easily one of the best spots for both, and my new favorite place to set up in a fresh save.

(Image credit: Pocketpair) (Image credit: Pocketpair) Image 1 of 2 View Original

The Sunlit Isle (405, -483) Pros: Several crude oil nodes, easy to defend during raids Cons: No nearby ore Closest teleport: Sunlit Isle It's not the best spot for ore or stone, but the Sunlit Isle just east of Palworld's starting area makes early game crude oil farming a breeze with six nodes scattered across the land. It's not difficult to defend, and the pals living here are under level 10. I like building at the highest point along the island's south side, but there's a cute spot northeast with stone steps leading up to it that works just as well. Even if you intend to go elsewhere for ore farming, this is a great place to build a second base for a steady crude oil supply.

items.title: v1.0.3: Balance Adjustments & Bug Fixes
items.summary: \ Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released! ＝＝＝ \ ▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon. ・Changed the t
items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released!

＝＝＝

\

▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon.

・Changed the technology unlock level of the Aquatic Construction Kit from Level 66 to Level 23, changed its Ancient Technology Point requirement from 4 to 1, and adjusted the required materials and work amount.

・Extended the duration of World Tree Holy Water.

・Reduced the weight of World Tree Holy Water from 1 to 0.1.

・Added World Tree Holy Water to the rewards for World Tree expeditions, World Tree fishing, and the Large Fishing Pond.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

・Fixed an issue where items could duplicate when performing certain actions.

・Fixed an issue where, when Katress's Partner Skill activated, switching spheres while riding could allow the player to obtain a different type of sphere.

・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Holy Water effect did not display correctly on the Pal being ridden when using World Tree Holy Water while riding.

・Fixed an issue where, after the World Tree Holy Water effect ended, riding a Pal would cause the World Tree Holy Water aura to reappear and not disappear when approaching trees in The World Tree area.

・Fixed an issue where an unintended reward was set for the desert expedition.

・Fixed an issue where the Dark Skill Fruit: Psycho Gravity did not appear on the item search screen.

・Fixed a bug where the firing interval was not set for sphere launchers

▼UI, Display, and Text

・Fixed an issue where resolution settings would not apply correctly in fullscreen mode.

・Fixed an issue where, after switching window mode with F11 / Alt+Enter, the game could unintentionally return to fullscreen mode after loading.

items.title: Palworld Is Getting an Official MMO Before Pokémon Later This Year
items.summary: Garena and Pocketpair have officially announced Palworld Online, a new mobile MMORPG that expands the creature-collecting survival hit into a persistent online world long before Pokémon has any indication of getting an official MMO of its own.
items.content:
Garena and Pocketpair have officially announced Palworld Online, a new mobile MMORPG that expands the creature-collecting survival hit into a persistent online world long before Pokémon has any indication of getting an official MMO of its own.

Palworld Sees New Surge of Players After Exiting Early Access

The Palworld universe is expanding once again, but this time into the MMO space. Garena and Pocketpair have officially announced Palworld Online , a new mobile MMORPG scheduled to launch later this year on iOS and Android.

The project marks the franchise's biggest expansion since Palworld reached its 1.0 release last month, reimagining the survival crafting experience as a persistent online world built around large-scale multiplayer exploration, creature collecting, and cooperative gameplay.

And this is all happening long before Pokémon has any semblance of an official MMO project of its own on the horizon.

While Pokémon Champions remains on the horizon, Palworld Online will become the first official massively multiplayer creature-collecting experience from either franchise to launch later this year, bringing persistent online progression, guilds, and large-scale social features to Pocketpair's breakout IP. Other games like TemTem beat them both to the punch.

According to Garena, the new game preserves the "core pillars" that helped make the original game a global phenomenon. Players will explore an expansive open world, capture and train Pals, gather resources, build bases, and craft equipment while taking on both cooperative PvE content and competitive PvP encounters. The mobile adaptation also introduces an original narrative setting featuring exclusive story content and side quests created specifically for Palworld Online.

Rather than serving as a direct port, the game has been redesigned around mobile devices. Garena says the interface has been rebuilt with touch controls in mind, including optional one-tap management features intended to streamline base building and routine tasks without sacrificing the freedom and exploration that defined the original release.

The announcement follows a busy year for the franchise. In July, Palworld officially exited Early Access with its massive 1.0 update, adding a new story chapter, the floating Sunreach region, dozens of new Pals, expanded progression systems, multiplayer improvements, and extensive overhauls across graphics and base building. The update also brought the total Pal roster to nearly 300 creatures.

Garena has not yet announced a specific release date beyond a 2026 launch window, but players can now pre-register and follow development through the game's official channels. Other forthcoming games from Pocketpair include the Pal♡world! dating sim and Palworld: Palfarm farming sim.
